attack_surfaces.operation: call rax (indirect call to user-controlled RWX mmap base)
attack_surfaces.reason: User-supplied bytes are read directly into an RWX anonymous mmap page and then executed via 'call rax'. This is a deliberate shellcode execution challenge. The seccomp filter is the primary constraint: only open/openat/read(fd==4)/mmap/fstat/brk/exit/exit_group are allowed; write is blocked, so shellcode must use open+read(fd==4) to exfiltrate data (e.g. flag file).

attack_surfaces.operation: seccomp_rule_add with arg0==4 filter on read syscall
attack_surfaces.reason: read() is only allowed when fd==4. Shellcode must open() a file (returns fd 3 typically) and then either dup to fd 4 or open a second file to reach fd 4 before read. This is the core puzzle for S2/S3/S4 to reason about.

No RPATH/RUNPATH in binary; libseccomp resolved from system path /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. LD_LIBRARY_PATH would take priority if set, allowing potential library substitution — but this is a standard runtime fact, not a binary vulnerability.
